title: GitLab Pricing in 2026: What Teams Pay
summary: Gitlab pricing tiers determine which DevOps features and automation limits are available for your development team.
body_markdown:
## Gitlab pricing plans and feature limits


Tier Price (Per User/Mo) CI/CD Minutes Max Users Key Features


Free $0 400 mins 5 users Basic CI/CD


Premium $29 10,000 mins Unlimited Advanced CI/CD, Code Reviews


Ultimate $99 50,000 mins Unlimited Vulnerability Management, Compliance


Small groups find the Free tier to be a cul-de-sac. The Premium and Ultimate tiers capture margin from growing organizations that require increased compute overhead for automated pipelines.


### The Free tier for individual contributors


The Free tier is a restricted environment where the primary constraint is the hard cap on the number of collaborators allowed in a private namespace.


Because this tier limits a group to five users, you're forced to migrate to a paid plan the moment you hire a sixth employee, even if your technical requirements haven't changed.


### Deployment models and user limits


The five-user restriction is a specific commercial lever applied only to the GitLab SaaS (GitLab.com) offering. This limitation serves as a gate to push small cloud-hosted teams into the paid Premium tier as soon as they achieve any organizational momentum.


If you choose to host the software on your own infrastructure, the self-managed Core version allows for unlimited users at no cost.


This creates a hidden operational tax where you must choose between paying for seat licenses or bearing the internal engineering overhead of maintaining your own server.


### Tier rebranding and feature parity


GitLab recently renamed the self-managed Core tier to GitLab Free. While this version removes the user cap found on the SaaS Free plan, it does not grant access to the advanced capabilities found in higher tiers.


Self-hosting only unlocks the basic feature set for a larger group. If your team requires merge request approvals or protected branches, you must still pay for a Premium subscription even when running the software on your own hardware.


**400 monthly CI/CD minutes** means if you're running a standard suite of tests on every commit, you'll likely exhaust your compute quota mid-month, leaving your team unable to automate deployments for the remainder of the billing period, which forces developers to wait until the next cycle to push updates.


This halts all automated deployments unless you purchase additional credits or upgrade your subscription.


### Premium for scaling development teams


Premium is the baseline for professional engineering organizations, removing the user ceiling to allow for departmental growth.


Tracker notes that by increasing the monthly CI/CD allowance to 10,000 minutes, GitLab provides enough compute for active development cycles, ensuring that high-frequency testing no longer triggers a service lockout.


**$29 per user per month** is the cost of this transition, so organizations must re-evaluate their total headcount expenses before committing to the upgrade. You must weigh the benefit of increased automation against the impact on your operational budget.


This tier introduces features like protected branches and merge request approvals. These are necessary for maintaining code quality in environments where multiple developers contribute to the same repository.


A flat 1 credit per flow run is how[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) decouples operational logic from the per-step compute costs that drive GitLab upgrades.


Because every flow run consumes exactly one credit regardless of its complexity, builders can break work into the granular, reliable steps good automation requires without being taxed for the precision of the build.


### GitLab Ultimate plan pricing and features


Ultimate targets organizations that must satisfy external auditors or manage large-scale security risks across hundreds of repositories.


The jump to $99 per user per month is justified by the inclusion of vulnerability management and compliance dashboards, which means security teams can centralize their oversight without needing additional third-party software.


A centralized view of security flaws discovered during the build process is provided by these tools. This reduces the time you spend manually auditing code for regulatory requirements.


By bundling **50,000 CI/CD minutes** , this tier supports the heavy compute demands of advanced static and dynamic analysis tools.


For a team of 100 developers, this represents a significant annual investment. It may include a vast array of portfolio management tools that smaller, agile teams find redundant to their existing stack.
